title: Judge Gaynor and Danny Barker, banjoists who came and went
summary: Gaynor and Barker rarely stayed in New Orleans; Verrett rehearsed with Barker and saw him in New York in 1959.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You didn't have Judge Gaynor in that band?

No, Judge wasn't in that band then. He wasn't in the band with us then. Judge, uh, Judge, uh, he didn't stay in New Orleans that much. He'd mostly be in and out, he'd mostly be here in New York City. He's a good banjo player.
He traveled up to Mississippi for a while, with little brother Montgomery and another group.
Yeah, he didn't stay here much. George was very seldom, I mean, you'd catch him now and the next thing you know he's gone, like Danny Barker, you know. They'd go out and just move abroad.
Yeah, we never think much about Danny Barker, he's been gone so many years. Do you remember when he played around here?

Yeah, he stood here quite a while. I used to rehearse with him. He called me up and would go up to his house and we'd sit on it. He had two six-string banjos. He promised me one I didn't pick up on at the time, so he gave it away to someone else. He's a wonderful banjo musician too. I saw him in New York in 59. I spent a couple days with him at his house.
